next_note: **P4-03 is done and the demo path is one command per step** (D-060, D-061). The integrity work is `cap/integrity.py`: a per-entry sha256 index with a sorted root, four findings (edited entry, missing entry, unlisted entry, malformed line), and a `verify` that every reader shares; the acceptance line was run on a real capsule with one byte flipped in `events/seg-000001.raw` and `blackbox verify` printed `events/seg-000001.raw: sha256 a7d760... does not match the recorded f9271593...` and exited 9. Alongside it, three things that blocked a usable release were fixed rather than planned: **capsules were 16 MiB each** because recovery shipped the whole preallocated segment (now 9.8 KiB for the same five-frame run, with the zeros dropped and any non-zero tail kept as evidence; the first attempt cut into a frame whose payload ended in zeros and `derived_parts` caught it immediately); **`pip install -e .` produced no `blackbox` command** because `[project.scripts]` was never declared; and **`blackbox ls`/`verify --data` looked in `./.blackbox` while `run` writes into the current directory**, so the command a new user types after a run said "no capsules". `blackbox ls` (manifest-only, `--json`, unreadable capsules listed with the reason) and a rewritten README whose console blocks are pinned by `tests/test_readme.py` complete the front door. The four-command path was run end to end for this commit: a real `openai` 3.51.0 client under `blackbox run` produced 23- and 17-event capsules, `ls` listed them, `diagnose` wrote a report with one `observed` finding, `view` wrote a 56 KB page, `verify` exited 0, and `repair preview` -> `apply --approve <token>` -> `verify --test` applied a fix and reported PASS. **P4-05 is only partial**: `ls` exists, the clause "every command has `--json`" is not met. **P3B-03 remains open with 0 node-level edges and defect 58 remains open with no universal 100 ms claim.** Next: **P4-04**, the 12-case attack corpus against the capsule reader (right code, under 50 ms). **CI on `127d187` was red on all nine cells and the two causes are fixed (D-062, D-063, defect 60).** The suite-count sentence said 1146 because it was measured without `anthropic`; CI installs `.[dev,capture,capture-sdks]` and collects 1162, and the test now says which environment the number belongs to (and skips, naming the package, when one is absent) instead of comparing against a number it cannot check. The second red was a **103.2 ms watchdog outage** on ubuntu py3.11: the rebind itself took 103.04 ms while seven other samples took 0.3 ms, because `rebind()` waited on a `run_coroutine_threadsafe(...).result()` for a loop thread the runner had descheduled (86.2 ms of tick lateness in the same run). The notice now repairs the listener **on the loop thread**, removing the hop; the budget is still 100.0 ms asserted on every sample, the tick still covers silent deaths, and the test starts its clock when `close()` returns (before that the listener was still accepting) and prints the harness's own `dispatch_ms` beside the outage. Measured after: 0.0-0.75 ms outages, 0.14-0.40 ms rebinds, 8/8 restores from the loop. Re-measured after the fix with `bench/bench_rebind.py --n 60`: gate PASS, 240 samples, worst outage 21.185 ms, 0 over budget, 0 port moves (`bench/results/2026-11-17-rebind-after-loop-restore.json`); the notice path moved from p50 0.919 to 0.459 ms of outage (idle) and 0.721 to 0.141 ms (loaded). **The outage is now measured by requests, not by a coroutine's return (defect 60, D-063).** The previous clock started when `close()` returned, which cannot see downtime that happens *inside* `close()`: the listening socket stops accepting before the caller is woken. `tools/rebind_probe.py` issues a real request in a tight loop on the port the child was told and reports the interval from the first request that was not served to the first one that was; `outage_upper_ms` (last served before, first served after) is the conservative bound the 100 ms budget is asserted on, and the probe's own resolution is printed beside it. `tests/test_rebind_probe.py` stalls `close()` for 60 ms after the socket closed and asserts the clock contains it (60.86 ms measured, against ~0 ms from a post-`close()` clock). Request-level bench: `bench/results/2026-11-17-rebind-request-level.json`, 240 samples, gate PASS, worst upper bound 42.762 ms, 0 over budget, 0 port moves. Two shortcuts were measured and rejected: a connect-only probe (a closed listening socket keeps completing handshakes from its accept queue, so 46 ms of a 60 ms stall looked like service) and a fixed 10 ms answer cap (every attempt on a Windows runner answers in ~16 ms, so the probe reported that a serving listener was not serving); the cap is now calibrated per machine and recorded with each sample.
